newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria Social Democrats soar to post-1994 high.
newsitem.headline: Austria Social Democrats soar to post-1994 high.

text.p: Austria's Social Democrats scored their highest approval rating for two and a half years in an opinion poll published on Monday, two weeks after Viktor Klima agreed to take over as chancellor and party leader.

The survey, conducted by the ISMA research institute and printed in Profil current affairs magazine, showed backing for the Social Democrats at 41 percent, up eight percent since mid-December and 12 percent since European parliamentary elections in October.
The Social Democrats last breached the 40 percent mark in the summer of 1994.

Sixty percent of the 500 voters interviewed by IMAS said they would elect Klima as chancellor. The former finance minister was named as Franz Vranitzky's successor on January 18 and formally sworn in on January 28.
The conservative People's Party, junior partner in the two-party coalition, saw its share of the vote drop to 23 percent from 30 percent in the European election.
The opposition far-right Freedom Party also scored 23 percent, down from 28 percent in October.
The leftist Greens and Liberal Forum were steady at six and five percent respectively.
